name: Heading levels not skipped (h1 → h2 → h3, no jumps)
source: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A) + /rams Moderate tier
description: Checks the heading outline for skipped levels (e.g., h1 followed directly by h3, or no h1 at all). Screen readers expose headings as a navigable structure, so skipped levels confuse the document outline.
rationale: WCAG SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships, Level A) requires that 'information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined.' The heading hierarchy is the primary skim/navigation structure for screen reader users. The /rams design review classifies skipped heading levels as a Moderate accessibility issue. A page should have exactly one h1 (the page topic) and h2-h6 should follow without skipping.
pass_criteria: Exactly one h1 element exists, and traversing the headings in document order never increases the level by more than 1 (h1 → h2 OK; h2 → h3 OK; h2 → h4 NOT OK).
